notes: Sweep run via four parallel lane agents (ai/bigtech/devtools/security), then cross-checked every candidate against the existing corpus by hand before filing. All direct WebFetch attempts to primary domains (anthropic.com, ces.tech, cisa.gov, endoflife.date, github.blog) hit EGRESS_BLOCKED as usual; filed entries are sourced from search results that quoted or cited the organisation's own page, or reputable secondary reporting when the org's own page wasn't reachable. Most of the lane agents' 'correction' candidates turned out to already be fully and correctly on file (CES 2027, AWS re:Invent, KubeCon NA and Europe, IFA Berlin, Meta Connect, Black Hat USA, NVIDIA GTC, RSA Conference, Let's Encrypt cert lifetime, and the Gemini Robotics ER 1.6 shutdown date) - refiling those with slightly different title/org wording risked creating fresh duplicate rows (apply-findings' id/dedupe keys are sensitive to exact org-string matches) for zero informational gain, so they were dropped. Filed genuine confidence upgrades only where the new source materially improved on what's already recorded: Microsoft Ignite 2026, NeurIPS 2026 and DEF CON 35 (expected -> confirmed, each via the organisation's own page/account) and ICLR 2027 (rumored/month-precision -> confirmed with an exact day range, via iclr.cc). Titles/orgs for those four were matched verbatim to the existing entries to guarantee a clean merge rather than a duplicate. Dropped three single-source, rumored Apple hardware-date leaks (iPhone 18 Pro pre-order/retail, OLED iPad mini) and a Google Cloud Next 2027 candidate whose only source was an ambiguous 2026-event FAQ page, as below the inclusion bar. Filed 'Microsoft Patch Tuesday - September 2026' with the month in the title (matching the pattern already used for November/December/January) specifically to avoid apply-findings' generic-title + 75-day-drift tolerance silently merging it into the existing October entry, a dedup gap flagged in prior runs' notes and still unresolved in apply-findings/id.ts. The existing corpus still carries unresolved near-duplicate rows for CES 2027, NeurIPS 2026, AWS re:Invent 2026, KubeCon NA/Europe and RSA Conference 2027 (flagged by prior runs); this run's corrections were deliberately id-matched to only one of each pair since data/ can't be hand-edited to merge them outright.
